tail(dowsing,4)

# Task 2 {-}

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Fit the linear model
ylm <- lm(PIPE ~ GUESS, data = dowsing)
summary(ylm)

# Create the ggplot
ggplot(dowsing, aes(x = GUESS, y = PIPE)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
```


$$\widehat{\text{PIPE}} = `r round(coef(ylm)[1], 4)` + `r round(coef(ylm)[2], 4)` \cdot \text{GUESS}$$


# Task 3 {-}


```{r}
# create data frame 
res_df <- data.frame(
  yhat_i = fitted(ylm),
  r_i = residuals(ylm)
)

# create plot 
ggplot(res_df, aes(x = yhat_i, y = r_i)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess") +
  labs(
    title = "Diagnostic plot",
    x = "yhat_i",
    y = "r_i"
  )
```

```{r}
library(s20x)
# call function 
normcheck(ylm, shapiro.wilk = TRUE)
```


Normality (from normcheck): The points on the Q-Q plot closely follow the straight diagonal reference line, and the histogram of residuals appears roughly bell-shaped and symmetric. Additionally, the Shapiro-Wilk test yields a high p-value (W = 0.9869, p = 0.978), meaning we do not reject the null hypothesis of normality—the normality assumption for the errors is well satisfied.   

Linearity & Constant Variance (from the Diagnostic Plot): The residuals are scattered fairly randomly around the horizontal 0 line without a strong funnel shape (supporting constant variance/homoscedasticity), though the loess curve shows a slight wave/dip around y hat approx 55, suggesting minor non-linearity or influence from a few spread-out observations.

# Task 5 {-}

H0: beta 1 = 0 versus Ha: beta 1 does not equal 0 to evaluate whether there is evidence that dowsers divine water (if dowsers have no genuine ability beyond random guessing, there is no linear relationship between GUESS and PIPE, so beta 1 = 0).

The 95% confidence interval for GUESS beta 1 is [-0.0843, 0.7000] (exact: -0.08427417 to 0.6999993). Because 0 falls inside this interval, we fail to reject H0.

p-value and alpha = 0.05: The GUESS p-value (Pr(>|t|)) is 0.1182. Because 0.1182 > 0.05, we fail to reject H0.

Rejection Region RR and T stat: With 24 degrees of freedom at alpha = 0.05, the critical value is t crit approx 2.0639 (2.063899), giving a two-tailed rejection region of T > 2.0639 or T < -2.0639. Your calculated test statistic is T calc = 1.620 (t value for GUESS). Because 1.620 < 2.0639, T calc is not in the rejection region, so we fail to reject H0. 



All three methods fail to reject H0, so there is insufficient statistical evidence at alpha = 0.05 to conclude that dowsers divine water. 

```{r}
summary(ylm)
confint(ylm, level = 0.95)

t_crit <- qt(1 - 0.05 / 2, df = ylm$df.residual)
t_crit
```

```{r}
# Load data
spruce <- read.csv("SPRUCE.csv")
head(spruce)

# function to calculate piecewise regression
myf2 <- function(x, xk1, xk2, coef) {
  coef[1] + coef[2]*(x) + 
    coef[3]*(x - xk1)*(x > xk1) + 
    coef[4]*(x - xk2)*(x > xk2)
}

# Function to extract coefficients using indicator variables for knots
coeff <- function(xk1, xk2) {
  df <- within(spruce, {
    x1 <- (BHDiameter - xk1) * (BHDiameter > xk1)
    x2 <- (BHDiameter - xk2) * (BHDiameter > xk2)
  })
  lsp <- lm(Height ~ BHDiameter + x1 + x2, data = df)
  coef(lsp)
}

#  Base R Plot of Spruce Data
with(spruce, plot(BHDiameter, Height,
                     pch = 21,
                     cex = 1.5,
                     bg = "green",
                     main = "Height Vs BHDiameter using piecewise regression"
))

# Add the fitted piecewise regression curve with knots at 10 and 18
cf <- coeff(10, 18)
curve(myf2(x, 10, 18, cf), add = TRUE, lwd = 2, col = "blue")
```


# Task 6 {-}

```{r}
# call function
myknot(x_k = 17, x = spruce$BHDiameter, y = spruce$Height)
```
```{r}
# assign values to variables 
diam <- spruce$BHDiameter
height <- spruce$Height
nvalues <- 1000
x <- seq(min(diam), max(diam), length = nvalues)
y <- vector(mode = "numeric", length = nvalues)

# create for loop
for (i in 1:nvalues) {
  y[i] <- myknot(x[i], x = diam, y = height)
}

# assign to variable 
nmax <- which.max(y)
plot(x, y, type = "l", lwd = 1.2, col = "Red",
     xlab = "x_k (Knot Position)", ylab = "R-squared",
     main = "R-squared vs. Knot Position")
abline(v = x[nmax], lwd = 3)
```
```{r}
# Grid search maximum
x_k <- x[nmax]
myknot(x_k = x_k, x = diam, y = height)
x_k

# Exact numerical optimization over [15, 20]
optimize(myknot, interval = c(15, 20), x = diam, y = height, maximum = TRUE)
```
